answer: Each epoch, every identity is drafted for jury duty: it grades a stranger's answer, scored against a rotating panel's consensus. Jurors voting with the majority earn standing; careless votes cost it, and repeated misses freeze it. Grading well demands attention, so one operator running many clones cannot staff every seat — the workload is the cost. Like a cipher that only opens when every tumbler aligns, only identities that do the work are admitted. A jetty reaches open water one stone at a time; standing accrues the same way, and the terrace of earned verdicts stays visible to all.
